uncited: This family encompasses methods that convert implicit neural radiance fields (NeRFs) or signed distance fields (SDFs) into explicit polygonal mesh representations or duplex surface structures.
It solves the problem of high computational cost and lack of explicit geometric topology in volumetric NeRFs by replacing dense ray sampling with surface intersections or deformable anchor grids.

It differs from sibling methods like [I2-SDF](18170-i2-sdf.md) and [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md) by prioritizing explicit mesh extraction or duplex surface approximation for real-time rendering, rather than optimizing a continuous SDF field for volume rendering integration.
This scalar field is transformed into opacity $\alpha$ or density $\sigma$ for volume rendering integration.
**Laplacian CDF (Standard SDF):** Used in [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md).
where $\beta$ controls the tightness of the surface representation [18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md].
where $d(\mathbf{x})$ is the SDF value and $\beta$ is a learnable sparsity parameter [18170-i2-sdf.md].
To sample points efficiently near the surface, methods like [SDF-based Volume Rendering with Laplacian CDF](18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md) use inverse CDF sampling.

Random numbers $u_i \in [0, 1]$ are generated and transformed to sample distances $t_i$ using the inverse of the CDF $\Phi^{-1}(u_i)$, concentrating samples near the zero-crossing of the SDF [18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md].
Stratification is applied by dividing the unit interval into bins [18174-sdf-based-volume-rendering-with-laplacian-cdf.md].
As seen in [UniSurf](#unisurf), an occupancy field acts as an indicator of surface presence.
Subsequent developments like NeuDA and NDRF extended these principles to address specific limitations in spatial encoding efficiency and rendering speed, respectively.
